cards.title: Advertorials Split Selling Pressure With the Ad
cards.summary: Use an advertorial as a second force in the funnel so the ad doesn't have to carry all the selling to purchase.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to send ad traffic to a plain product page or to an advertorial/landing page before checkout.
steps: Map the buying journey as a continuum from first ad impression to purchase; every funnel element exists to move the audience along it.
Recognize that a basic product page (benefits, product photos, trust elements) leaves all selling power sitting on the ad alone.
Add an advertorial so two forces push the prospect forward: the ad and the landing page.
Use the advertorial's editorial disguise to educate, handle objections, and intensify desire in a low-pressure, low-stakes environment where people engage as they would an article.
Write the copy well enough that by the bottom of the page the reader simply wants to buy.
caveats: Advertorials are framed by the source as amplifiers of already-winning messaging, not a fix for unvalidated offers or weak creative.

cards.title: Validate Four Ad-Level Variables Before Building the Advertorial
cards.summary: Confirm avatar, desire, angle and unique mechanism at the ad level before investing in an advertorial landing page.
cards.use_when: Planning a new campaign or product launch and deciding whether it's safe to build an advertorial now.
steps: Test messaging on the ad level first to get confirmation of four variables: avatar, desire, angle, and unique mechanism.
Look for at least break-even conversion to a product page — the source cites break-even on roughly $1,000 of spend as sufficient confirmation, though any break-even signal works.
Build the advertorial once those four variables are proven, so the landing page amplifies messaging that already converts.
Extract each variable from a live winning ad: identify who the avatar is, the plainly stated problem/desire, and the named mechanism with its explanation.

Example structure from the source: avatar = retired senior men with sciatica; problem/desire = sciatica pain relief; mechanism = a physical-therapist-explained spinal decompression home device that stretches the spine and forces fluid back into bulging discs.
caveats: Source states this isn't an absolute rule, but in the overwhelming majority of cases launching an advertorial before testing any ads is unlikely to convert.
Break-even thresholds are the presenter's heuristic, not a universal benchmark.

cards.title: Choose Advertorial Style by Product Type: Improvement vs Innovation
cards.summary: Match advertorial format to whether your product is a better version of a known product or a brand-new innovation.
cards.use_when: Selecting the advertorial angle and length for a product before writing any copy.
steps: Classify the product as an improvement product (a better version of something buyers already know) or an innovation/gadget (something the market hasn't seen or considered as a solution).
For improvement products, lead with personal stories of people who solved their problem after trying and failing with other products in the category.
For innovations, use a breaking-news or big-revelation frame (e.g. 'revolutionary device'), which lets you get straight into selling faster.
Then layer awareness level on top: consider the mindset of someone who just consumed your ad and pick an advertorial style that fits that awareness.
Don't copy a random advertorial from another product type — one advertorial style does not work for all products.
caveats: The source presents these style-fit observations as its own testing experience, not a controlled benchmark.

cards.title: Match Advertorial Length to How Much Selling the Ad Already Did
cards.summary: Apply the selling-pressure continuum: less selling in the ad means a longer advertorial; more selling in the ad means a shorter, more direct one.
cards.use_when: Writing an advertorial lead length and deciding how soon to reveal the product, based on the current ad creative.
steps: Assess how much selling your ad creative does. Clickbait image ads that only sell the click (little or no body copy) do almost no selling.

If the ad does little selling, build a long advertorial with a long lead: remind the audience of the problem, agitate the pain, intensify desire, then introduce the product. In the source's example the reader scrolls roughly 50–60% of the page before realizing a product is being sold.

If the ad already sells heavily — long-form personal stories, 1,000–3,000-word sales letters, 1–2 minute UGC videos, or 4–5 minute VSLs — write a shorter advertorial with a shorter lead and cut to the product sooner.
Show the product early on the page (e.g. in the top image and the first few lines) when the ad has already done the persuading.
State the paradigm explicitly: less selling on the ad means more selling on the lander; more selling on the ad means less on the lander.
caveats: The presenter calls this 'not always true, but true the overwhelming majority of the time' — treat it as a heuristic, not a fixed rule.

cards.title: Swipe Proven Advertorial Structures From Affiliate Hubs
cards.summary: Source advertorial structures from affiliate advertorial hubs, ideally from outside your own niche, to gain a structural edge.
cards.use_when: Looking for a proven advertorial layout to model before writing your own.
steps: Use affiliate advertorial hubs — pages aggregating many advertorials across niches — as a swipe library because they hold a high quantity and wide variety of advertorials.
Pick one that matches your product type; same-niche picks give extra confidence it already converts for a similar product.
Deliberately look outside your niche too: marketers in one niche often copy each other, so importing structures or avatar treatments from other niches can be genuinely differentiating.

Note the structure you intend to replicate (urgency banner, curiosity headline, author intro, problem, agitation, product reveal, mechanism, quality, social proof, price justification) so you can instruct the AI to mirror it.
caveats: Same-niche swipes are a confidence boost, not a requirement; the source explicitly says it doesn't always have to be in the niche.
Treat swiped structures as formats to adapt, not copy to publish verbatim.

cards.title: Claude Advertorial Workflow: PDFs In, HTML Out
cards.summary: Feed Claude a full-page competitor advertorial PDF, an Amazon product-page PDF, and your four validated variables to get a structured advertorial in HTML.
cards.use_when: Producing a first-draft advertorial page for a Shopify store quickly, once the four ad-level variables are validated.
steps: Capture the competitor advertorial you want to swipe as a full-page PDF using a screen-capture extension (the source uses Ghost full-page capture).
Go to Amazon, find your exact product or a close equivalent, expand all highlights and feature sections, and capture that page as a PDF too.
Attach both PDFs to Claude and state the product you sell plus the goal: recreate the example advertorial's structure for your product.
Supply the four validated variables explicitly (avatar, desire, problem, unique mechanism) and instruct Claude to keep them consistent because they are proven winning ad messaging.
Ask for the advertorial output in pure HTML, exactly mirroring the example structure.
Note the source's own run took about 6 minutes 41 seconds, not the advertised 5 minutes.
caveats: Do not invent the four variables for a real campaign; the source does so only for demonstration and explicitly says you should use confirmed ones.
Claude's output still needs edits — headline tweaks, lead adjustments, mechanism phrasing, and real images.
Tool interfaces and available models change; verify the current capture extension and chat interface before relying on this exact flow.

cards.title: Deploy Advertorial HTML on Shopify via PageFly Custom HTML Block
cards.summary: Paste Claude-generated advertorial HTML into a blank page builder page with hidden header and footer for instant Shopify deployment.
cards.use_when: Publishing a generated advertorial to a Shopify store and needing it to render as a standalone editorial page.
steps: Create a blank page using a page builder such as PageFly.
Add a custom HTML section/block to that page.
Upload/paste the full advertorial HTML from Claude into the custom HTML block.
Hide the theme's header and footer so the page reads as a standalone editorial rather than a store page.
Use the page builder's page list to keep track of all advertorial pages.
The source notes a native free Shopify route likely exists, but the page builder is preferred for header/footer control and page management.
caveats: PageFly specifics and any free Shopify alternative may change; verify the current app interface and block naming before building the workflow around it.
Input real product images and make final edits rather than shipping raw AI output.

input.text:
07-LPG / landing pages and funnels Goes here. A breakdown of how to use AI (specifically Claude) to generate direct-response advertorials in under seven minutes. It covers the strategy of matching advertorial length to the ad source, extracting winning variables (avatar, desire, angle, mechanism) from ad accounts, and using HTML generation for rapid deployment on Shopify. Not here. • Technical setup of Shopify stores or basic theme customization -> 05-SET • Facebook Ads media buying or campaign scaling strategies -> 10-MCR

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a rapid, AI-driven workflow for generating high-converting advertorials, explaining the crucial strategy of aligning the advertorial's length and "selling pressure" inversely with the front-end ad. modules: [LPG] topics: [advertorials, landing page design, AI copywriting, Claude, direct response, funnel congruency, unique mechanism, Shopify, PageFly] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. the purpose of an advertorial / explaining that advertorials split the "selling pressure" between the ad and the landing page, educating the customer and intensifying desire in a low-stakes, editorial-style environment; the prerequisite for advertorials / warning against building an advertorial blindly; instead, validating four variables (avatar, desire, angle, unique mechanism) at the ad level first to ensure the landing page amplifies already-winning messaging; ad-to-landing-page congruency / the critical rule that if an ad does very little selling (e.g., a clickbait image), the advertorial must be long and do heavy selling; conversely, if the ad is a long-form VSL or 3,000-word story, the advertorial should be shorter and cut straight to the product; swiping advertorial structures / utilizing affiliate advertorial hubs to find proven landing page structures outside of the immediate niche to gain a competitive edge; AI advertorial generation workflow / taking full-page PDF screenshots of a successful competitor's advertorial and an Amazon product page, uploading them to Claude, and prompting the AI to merge the competitor's structure with the validated four variables (avatar, problem, desire, mechanism); rapid deployment via HTML / prompting Claude to generate the final advertorial in pure HTML, allowing for instant deployment into a Shopify store using a custom HTML block in a page builder like PageFly to hide headers and footers.

Look for.

The "Selling Pressure" Continuum: The overarching funnel rule that if an ad does less selling (e.g., a clickbait image), the landing page must do more selling (a long-form advertorial). If the ad does heavy selling (e.g., a 5-minute VSL), the landing page should be shorter and more direct.

The Four Proven Variables: The prerequisite that before building an advertorial, a media buyer must validate four things at the ad level: the avatar, the core desire, the angle, and the unique mechanism.

The Claude HTML Workflow: The specific technical process of capturing full-page PDFs of a competitor's advertorial and a product page, feeding them into Claude, and instructing the AI to output the synthesized advertorial entirely in HTML for instant Shopify deployment.

Skip. The creator's 5-minute stopwatch challenge (which failed and took ~6.5 minutes), the promotional intro/outro hooks, and the hypothetical thought exercise about the "cat pee smell" product.

Scope mix. 20% baseline (basic definitions of advertorials and the four variables), 80% growth (advanced ad-to-page congruency rules and the AI/HTML rapid deployment workflow). Volume. ~400 words.
